sections.html: The Golden Panchax, Pachypanchax playfairii, is the only primary freshwater fish species from the Seychelles. It is one of the more robust killifish species and one of the comparatively rare killis that can be kept even in community tanks, although tankmates should not be too small. The maximum length reported in literature is 10 cm.

Aquarists who read older books find this killifish in all literature until the 1970s. Then the species seemed to disappear from the mainstream of the aquarium hobby. The specimens offered are tank-bred, bred in Europe.
It can be kept in community tanks, but tankmates should not be too small.
Females can be easily recognized by the dark spot in the dorsal fin.
In specimens ready to spawn the scales on the back ruffle up. This phenomenon is unique among all the fish species known so far.
Specimens are about 5 cm long and sexually fully mature.
